1. Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2.      To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

JUSTICE J.D. KAPOOR, PRESIDENT (ORAL)   Complainant purchased a machine (equipment) L & T 580-3, Loader Backhoe Hydraulic Excavator-cum-Loader machine Sl. No. ULB-2644, Engine No. 48.1505/0100203, Chasis No. ULB-01J264 of OP No.2 in the price of Rs. 14,15,000/- through its authorized dealer, OP No.1 on 04-12-2001.

The bill of the machine dated 15-12-2001 was delivered by OP No.2 to the complainant after three months, but form No. 21 (Sales Certificate) and form No. 22 (Initial Certificate of Road Worthiness) not given. OP No.2 gave both the forms No. 21 and 22 in April, 2002 to the complainant.

2. That OP No.3 financed Rs. 9,75,000/- at the interest rate of 9% p.a., out of Rs. 14,15,000/- to the complainant in December, 2001. The receipt of the cash was not issued by OP No.1 and 3 and they told that the above said money would be adjusted in bill. After receiving the full price of Rs. 14,15,000/- of the machine by OP No.2 he then delivered the machine to the complainant on 04-12-2001. The bill of the said machine was delivered to the complainant after three months by OP No.2.

3. That the above said machine started giving trouble on 02-05-2002 at evening. OP No.1 was informed by the complainant regarding the trouble of the machine on telephonic message on 03-05-2002 early morning. OP No.1 attended the complaint on 07-05-2002 and made entry of the working hour in service record as under:-

07-05-2002 - 509 hours 13-05-2002 - Entry not made 15-05-2002 - 517 hours 20-05-2002 - 552 hours 04-06-2002 - 619 hours 06-06-2002 - 619 hours 23-10-2002 - 1022 hours  

4. That defects developed during the period of warranty and machine was not working properly since 03-05-2002. The complainant made several complaints regarding the defect of the said machine. But OP No.1 did not find out the real defects in the said machine which was having persistent defect which could not be removed. The complainant also sent a message to OP No.2, Mr. K.V.S. Nair, who is a Senior Marketing Manager posted at Pithampur, M.P. in connection with the defect on above said machine by a fax 8292-56301 on 11-05-2002.

5. That the complainant discharged his liability by paying Rs. 5,51,000/- upto October, 2002 to OP No.3, while his machine was not functioning properly since 03-05-2002 and same was financed by OP No.3.

6. That on January 4/5, 2003 at night musclemen of OP No.3 were forcibly snatched the machine from the possession of the complainant at Mahipalpur, Rangpuri, Delhi by giving a informing letter to the operator of the machine. On 06-01-2003 when the complainant contact6ed OP No.3 about the incident, they had demanded Rs. 7,50,000/- full amount of loan plus Rs. 25,000/- other charges for hired musclemen deployed for the purpose.

7. That after the possession of the said machine Mr. Gauri Samant, Advocate, Bombay who was appointed as Arbitrator by OP No.3 sent a summon to the complainant dated 14-10-2004.

Complainant did not take part in the arbitration proceedings at Bombay because whole transaction was happened in Delhi and he was unable to bear the traveling and lodging expenditure at Bombay.

8. That OP No.3 filed a complaint against the complainant u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in the Honble Court of Ms. Poonam Chaudhry, M.M., Karkardooma, Delhi.

9. Complainant suffered heavy loss due to the defective machine delivered by OP No.2 and very poor service given by OP No.1. Complainant has claimed the following amount:-

(i) Cost of machine Sl. No. 2644 - Rs. 14,15,000/-
(ii) Salary of operator Rs. 10,000/- x 9 - Rs. 90,000/-
(iii) Salary of caretaker-cum-helper Rs.

8,000/- x 9 -

Rs. 72,000/-

(iv) Lawyer fee in the case u/s 138 NI Act Rs. 25,000/-

(v) Self communication expenditure in the case u/s 138 NI Act. - Rs. 20,000/-

(vi) Loss of Income - Rs. 1,20,000/-

(vii) Mental anguish and harassment - Rs. 3,00,000/-

(viii) Loss of business & credit name and fame in market and society - Rs. 4,58,000/-

10. OP No.2 who is the manufacturer of the machine was proceeded ex-parte whereas OP No.1 who is the dealer of OP No.2 has contested the claim of the complainant. According to OP No.1 its liability was limited being a dealer and whenever a machine was brought with some complaints of defects the said defects were removed. OP No.1 denied the allegation that it did not find out the real defects in the machine. Service Engineer of OP No.1 had visited complainants office on 02-05-2002, checked the machine, rectified the defect and after that the machine was working in satisfactory condition. Again on 06-05-2002 OP No.1 had received a call from complainant regarding the trouble of the machine and send their Service Engineer on 07-05-2002.

It was found that the MPR valve was failed and the machine was working but slow working, OP No.1 had immediately placed a warranty order on L & T for MPR valve. On 09-05-2002 OP No.1 had again send their Service Engineer along with MPR Valve but he was shocked and surprised to saw that the complainant was running their machine without Hydraulic Oil whereas it was strictly instructed by OP No.1 at the time of purchase that if you will run your machine without Hydraulic oil then it will damage the Hydraulic System.

11. Thus the complainant has no right to blame OP No.1 for the defect of the machine. On 09-05-2002 the Service Engineer of OP No.1 had came back from the complainants office and asked them to call only at that time when Hydraulic oil is available. After that OP No.1 had received a call from complainant on 11-05-2002 that they had purchased Hydraulic Oil. On 13-05-2002 OP No.1 had again sent their Service Engineer to rectify the defect and he was again shocked to saw the hydraulic oil because it was duplicate, local grade and adulterated oil, he refused to use that oil but customer forced to use that oil and then the Service Engineer used that oil with the condition that OP No.1 will not be responsible for the defect in their machine because of this oil and changed MPR Valve and checked all the functions of machine. After that the machine was working at satisfactory condition. Likewise several times OP No.1 had received complaint from the complainant, i.e. on 05-12-2001, 15-02-2002, 18-03-2002, 02-05-2002, 06-05-2002, 09-05-2002, 11-05-2002, 20-05-2002, 06-06-2002, 26-06-2002, 02-07-2002, 17-09-2002 and the same had always rectified by the Service Engineer of OP No.1.

12. The liability of the dealer is not of the same as that of the manufacturer. The dealer can be penalized only for not having not rendered satisfactory service and at the same time the dealer is also expected to ensure itself that the goods being sold by him is free from any manufacturing defect.

If a person purchases a brand new goods and takes the same every day to the dealer or its workshop for removing some or other defects then the consumer suffers heavily in terms of loss of business, mental agony, harassment, physical discomfort etc. It is not necessary for the consumer to prove the defect of the machine for replacement of the same with a new machine when the machinery suffers from inherent defect. Job card, number of times the consumes takes the defective goods to the manufacturer for rectifying the defect during the warranty period is sufficient to hold the goods as defective as defined by section 2(1)(f) of the Consumer Protection Act 1986.

13. In the given facts and circumstances of the case and after according careful consideration to the rival claims of the parties, we allow the complaint in the following terms:-

(i)                 OP No.1 shall pay compensation of Rs. 50,000/- for having put the complainant to mental agony, harassment for taking the machine time and again for removal of the defects.
(ii)               OP No.2 shall refund the entire cost of the machine to the complainant as he raised a loan from the bank @ 9% interest. Besides OP No.2 shall also pay Rs.

1,00,000/- as compensation for mental agony and harassment.

(iii)              So far as OP No.3 is concerned, it has taken away the machine without resorting to the legal remedy and also raised demand of the balance amount payable by the complainant. OP No.3 shall refund the amount of Rs. 4,40,000/- towards the margin money paid by the complainant while raising the loan and shall also pay Rs. 1,00,000/- as compensation for wrongful action.

14. Aforesaid order shall be complied with by the parties within one month from the date of receipt of this order.

15. Complaint is disposed of in aforesaid terms.

16. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.

17. Announced on the 23rd March, 2007     (Justice J.D. Kapoor) President     (Rumnita Mittal) jj Member
